assumptions.reason: Spec defines X as a parameter but states no numeric default; a value is required to run the strategy and is exposed as an overridable param.

assumptions.choice: Entry orders and the end-of-session exit order use exectype=bt.Order.Close
assumptions.reason: Spec requires fills 'at the close' of the bar on which the signal/exit condition occurs (09:45 close for entries, 15:45-16:00 close for EOD exit). Backtrader's default Market order fills at the next bar's open, so bt.Order.Close is the literal mechanism to realize a same-bar-close fill without altering harness-owned broker/cerebro settings (e.g., cheat-on-close).

assumptions.choice: 15-minute bars are assumed timestamped at period start, so the first regular bar of a session is stamped 09:30 and the last regular bar is stamped 15:45
assumptions.reason: The harness describes the dataset as starting at 09:30:00, consistent with start-of-period labeling; the spec itself names 09:45 and 15:45-16:00 explicitly, so day boundaries are detected via these fixed clock times rather than lookahead-dependent logic (which backtrader cannot support in next()).

assumptions.choice: No gap trade is taken on the first trading day in the dataset
assumptions.reason: Gap % requires a prior regular-session close, which does not exist before the first bar of the provided feed; no external/prior data is available.

assumptions.choice: If a position were opened on the final (partial) day in the dataset, no explicit 15:45 EOD-exit bar exists to trigger the scheduled close, so it would remain open until data ends and is resolved by the harness's normal end-of-backtest handling
assumptions.reason: The harness's stated data range ends mid-day (12:15) on the last date, so that session never reaches its normal 15:45 closing bar within the feed; this is an artifact of the fixed data window, not a strategy design choice.

assumptions.choice: No explicit leftover-position close-and-reverse branch is coded beyond a guard that skips new entries if a position is unexpectedly still open
assumptions.reason: Because the unconditional 15:45 EOD exit (via bt.Order.Close) resolves and is notified before the next day's first bar is processed, a prior day's position is always flat by the time the new day's gap is evaluated, so the reversal behavior is naturally satisfied by the ordinary close-then-enter sequencing.
